{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: run generator tests

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      pr_number:
        required: true
        type: number

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash -leo pipefail {0}

jobs:
  test-matrix:
    name: test matrix
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      test_names: ${{ steps.tests.outputs.test_names }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out pull request merge ref
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ inputs.pr_number }}/merge

      - name: Read generator test names
        id: tests
        run: |
          test_names="$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.dumps(sorted(json.load(open(".github/workflows/config/generator-tests.json")).keys())))')"
          echo "test_names=${test_names}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

  run-generator-test:
    name: ${{ matrix.test_name }}
    needs: test-matrix
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        test_name: ${{ fromJson(needs.test-matrix.outputs.test_names) }}
    env:
      DOCKER_DATA_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/.ci/docker
      FORCE_NON_EC2: 1
      JVM_OPTS: -Xmx3200m
    steps:
      - name: Maximize build space
        uses: jimfangx/maximize-build-space@master
        with:
          root-reserve-mb: 4096
          swap-size-mb: 10240
          remove-dotnet: 'true'
          remove-android: 'true'
          remove-haskell: 'true'
          remove-codeql: 'true'

      - name: Move Docker storage to workspace
        run: |
          sudo systemctl stop docker
          sudo mkdir -p "${DOCKER_DATA_ROOT}"
          printf '{ "data-root": "%s" }\n' "${DOCKER_DATA_ROOT}" | sudo tee /etc/docker/daemon.json
          sudo systemctl start docker
          docker info --format 'Docker root: {{ .DockerRootDir }}'

      - name: Pull Chipyard container
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          image_name="ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY,,}:main"
          echo "CHIPYARD_IMAGE=${image_name}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
          echo "${GITHUB_TOKEN}" | docker login ghcr.io -u "${GITHUB_ACTOR}" --password-stdin
          docker pull "${image_name}"

      - name: Run generator test in container
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr_number }}
          TEST_NAME: ${{ matrix.test_name }}
        run: |
          docker run --rm -i \
            --env "FORCE_NON_EC2=${FORCE_NON_EC2}" \
            --env "JVM_OPTS=${JVM_OPTS}" \
            --env "PR_NUMBER=${PR_NUMBER}" \
            --env "TEST_NAME=${TEST_NAME}" \
            --env "GITHUB_SERVER_URL=${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}" \
            --env "GITHUB_REPOSITORY=${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            "${CHIPYARD_IMAGE}" \
            bash -leo pipefail <<'CONTAINER_SCRIPT'
          cd /home/ubuntu/chipyard
          git config --global --add safe.directory "*"
          git remote set-url origin "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"

          # Record the submodules initialized in the pulled container.
          initialized_before="$(mktemp)"
          submodules_after="$(mktemp)"
          initialized_targets="$(mktemp)"
          new_targets="$(mktemp)"
          removed_targets="$(mktemp)"

          git submodule status \
            | awk 'substr($1, 1, 1) != "-" { print $2 }' \
            | sort -u > "${initialized_before}"

          # Checkout main in the container.
          git fetch --no-tags origin main
          git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD

          # Move to GitHub's current PR merge commit.
          git fetch --no-tags origin "pull/${PR_NUMBER}/merge"
          git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD

          # Compare submodule membership before and after the PR checkout.
          git config --file .gitmodules --get-regexp '^submodule\..*\.path$' \
            | awk '{ print $2 }' \
            | sort -u > "${submodules_after}"

          comm -12 "${initialized_before}" "${submodules_after}" > "${initialized_targets}"
          comm -13 "${initialized_before}" "${submodules_after}" > "${new_targets}"
          comm -23 "${initialized_before}" "${submodules_after}" > "${removed_targets}"

          # Remove submodules deleted by the PR.
          while read -r submodule_path; do
            [ -n "${submodule_path}" ] || continue
            git submodule deinit --force -- "${submodule_path}" || true
            rm -rf -- "${submodule_path}"
          done < "${removed_targets}"

          # Update submodules already initialized in the container.
          while read -r submodule_path; do
            [ -n "${submodule_path}" ] || continue
            git submodule sync -- "${submodule_path}"
            git submodule update --init -- "${submodule_path}"
          done < "${initialized_targets}"

          # Initialize submodules newly added by the PR.
          while read -r submodule_path; do
            [ -n "${submodule_path}" ] || continue
            git submodule init -- "${submodule_path}"
            git submodule sync -- "${submodule_path}"
            git submodule update --init -- "${submodule_path}"
          done < "${new_targets}"

          git rev-parse --short HEAD

          # Initialize only additional submodules needed by this generator test.
          bash .github/scripts/prepare-generator-test-submodules.sh "${TEST_NAME}" /home/ubuntu/chipyard

          # Build tests in both tests/ and tests/build due to legacy paths.
          source env.sh
          cmake -S tests -B tests/ -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
          cmake --build tests --target clean
          cmake --build tests --target all
          cmake -S tests -B tests/build -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
          cmake --build tests/build --target clean
          cmake --build tests/build --target all

          python3 .github/scripts/run-generator-test.py "${TEST_NAME}"
          CONTAINER_SCRIPT",
  "rationale": "The workflow's matrix job `run-generator-test` lacks an explicit timeout, relying on GitHub's default 6-hour limit. The job performs heavy operations (Docker pull, CMake configure/build, generator test execution) that could hang or run excessively long. Adding a custom timeout of 60 minutes bounds runaway consumption while allowing normal variation. This matches pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, which reports 12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction and has experimental evidence showing 26.8% elapsed savings. The timeout preserves all test coverage and behavior, only limiting maximum job duration.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}

The user wants me to analyze the provided workflow and evidence to propose a CI optimization. Let me first understand the workflow and then check the evidence for applicable patterns.

The workflow is `.github/workflows/run-generator-tests.yml` - it's a workflow_call that runs generator tests in a matrix. Key characteristics:
- Uses `workflow_call` trigger with `pr_number` input
- Has two jobs: `test-matrix` (reads test names) and `run-generator-test` (matrix job)
- The matrix job runs on `ubuntu-24.04` with `fail-fast: false`
- Uses Docker containers, pulls from GHCR
- Runs complex submodule management and CMake builds inside container
- Has `maximize-build-space` action to free up disk space

Now let me look at the evidence provided:

1. **P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE** (experiment example) - Shows adding pip cache to a Python workflow. Similarity 0.68. But this workflow uses Docker/CMake, not pip.

2. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** (experiment example) - Shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a Node.js workflow. Similarity 0.66. The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT in the catalogue has reported 12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction.

3. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** (experiment examples) - Shows changing `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true` in matrix strategies. Similarity ~0.65. The pattern P-LIT-FAIL-FAST has estimated 2% free / 1.5% paid VM time reduction.

4. **P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP** (experiment example) - Synthetic scenario, not directly applicable.

Looking at the workflow, I see:
- The `run-generator-test` job has `strategy: fail-fast: false` explicitly set
- No custom timeout is set on the job (uses GitHub's default 6 hours)
- The job runs complex Docker/CMake operations that could potentially hang

The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT seems applicable because:
- The workflow has no explicit timeout
- The job does heavy computation (CMake builds, generator tests) that could run long
- The pattern has evidence of 12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction
- The experiment example shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job

The pattern P-LIT-FAIL-FAST also seems applicable because:
- The workflow explicitly sets `fail-fast: false`
- The pattern suggests changing to `fail-fast: true` when matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable
- However, the contraindications include "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required"
- For generator tests, it's possible each test is independent and we want all results

Let me check the workflow more carefully. The matrix runs different generator tests. If one fails, do we need the others? The workflow doesn't seem to have a requirement that all must run. But the explicit `fail-fast: false` suggests they want all to run.

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, the preconditions are "Representative successful-duration history exists". We don't have that data, but the pattern is about bounding runaway jobs.

The evidence from the experiment example for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows a 26.8% elapsed savings. The pattern catalogue reports 12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction.

I think P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is the most applicable and safe optimization here. Adding a reasonable timeout to the matrix job would prevent runaway builds without changing the test behavior.

What timeout value? The experiment used 5 minutes for a Node.js lint/typecheck workflow. This workflow does heavy CMake builds and generator tests in Docker - likely takes longer. Looking at the workflow, it:
1. Maximizes build space
2. Moves Docker storage
3. Pulls Chipyard container
4. Runs generator test in container (includes git operations, submodule management, CMake configure/build, Python test script)

This could easily take 30-60 minutes. A reasonable timeout might be 60 minutes (1 hour) to allow for normal variation but catch truly stuck jobs.

However, I need to be careful - the instruction says "Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes." Adding a timeout doesn't change coverage, just bounds execution time.

Let me also consider P-LIT-FAIL-FAST. The workflow has `fail-fast: false` explicitly. Changing to `true` would cancel other matrix jobs on first failure. This could save time but might hide multiple failures. The pattern's contraindications include "Every matrix outcome is required" - for generator tests, we might want to see all failures. But the pattern has estimated benefit.

Given the evidence, I think P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is safer and has stronger evidence (12.9% reduction vs 2% for fail-fast). Also, the workflow currently has NO timeout, so adding one is a clear improvement.

I'll propose adding a `timeout-minutes: 60` to the `run-generator-test` job.

The evidence_ids should include the pattern catalogue entry for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and possibly the experiment example. The pattern catalogue document_id is "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT". The experiment example document_id is "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508".

I'll use both as evidence_ids.

Let me construct the updated workflow YAML. I need to add `timeout-minutes: 60` to the `run-generator-test` job (under the job definition, same level as `runs-on`).

Current job structure:
```yaml

    name: ${{ matrix.test_name }}
    needs: test-matrix
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        test_name: ${{ fromJson(needs.test-matrix.outputs.test_names) }}
    env:
      ...
    steps:
      ...
```

I'll add `timeout-minutes: 60` after `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`.
